parsed.explanation: From “V contains at most one positive number” alone, it does not follow that V is contained in {0,c}; negative values have not been excluded. The write-up later repeatedly relies on this unsupported classification, notably when Lemma 1 asserts b=g(z)∈{0,c}. The proposed repair is valid: if g(x₀)=-d<0, then (4) inductively gives g(x₀-nd)=-d and x₀-nd>0 for every n, because each next point equals f(x₀-(n-1)d)>0. But for n>x₀/d, x₀-nd≤0, a contradiction. Since this argument or an equivalent one appears nowhere in the write-up, the necessity proof is incomplete as written.
